title: sizeof and Number Types
instructions: Numbers come in different sizes for different jobs. sizeof tells you how much space a type uses, in bytes.
sizeof(int) is usually 4, a double 8, a char 1. Print the result with %zu.
- unsigned int — no negatives allowed, so it can hold a bigger positive number. Print with %u.
- long long — holds HUGE whole numbers. Print with %lld.
Pick the smallest type that comfortably fits your numbers.
task: Add the line that prints big with %lld, so the output ends with:  big = 10000000000
hint:
Use the %lld specifier for long long:

    printf("big = %lld\n", big);
expected_output:
int takes 4 bytes
char takes 1 bytes
big = 10000000000
